discovery: Squeezed light for beating the quantum limit in gravitational-wave interferometry
subfield: Quantum optics and precision measurement / gravitational-wave physics
motivation: Caves showed in 1981 that the quantum noise limiting laser interferometers comes from vacuum fluctuations entering the dark port, and that injecting squeezed vacuum could beat the so-called standard quantum limit. For decades this looked like a laboratory curiosity. Schnabel and coworkers developed stable, high-factor squeezed-light sources at audio frequencies and made squeezing operational at GEO600. Mavalvala led the effort to bring squeezing into LIGO, including frequency-dependent squeezing that reduced both shot noise and radiation-pressure noise in kilometre-scale detectors. Squeezing now runs routinely in LIGO and Virgo, raises the detection rate of black-hole and neutron-star mergers by tens of percent, and gave the first demonstration of quantum correlations acting on macroscopic, kilogram-scale mirrors. The work turned a fundamental quantum limit into an engineering parameter. It also founded a field of quantum-enhanced measurement that is spreading to dark-matter searches and tests of gravity.
